record.title: Ras Jedir January 2018 armed-conflict interruption and Tunisian outbound closure
record.direction: Explicit Tunisian outbound prohibition; Libyan-side disruption.
record.movement: Outbound travellers toward Libya; broader transit disrupted.
record.exceptions: Tunisians returning from Libya admitted; some Libyan arrivals also reported.
record.imposing_authority: Tunisian army outbound control; armed groups disputing Libyan post
record.enforcement: Army blocked outward routes while arrivals remained possible.
record.relationship: Promotes R2-AF-L002; separate from July–September 2018 NA009.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no present status inferred.
record.official_rationale: No formal order text recovered; contemporary reports connect closure with armed attack.
record.context: Libyan armed factions contested control; subsequent agreement assigned post security to presidential guard.
record.uncertainty: Libya Herald's January 6 contemporary report says the crossing reopened that afternoon; TAP reports resumed activity Sunday January 7. January 6 movement/direction is unspecified, so the Tunisian outbound endpoint is bounded January 6–7. TAP republications share one origin; no universal two-way closure or exact hourly duration is asserted.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope. No complete continuous operational interval established.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Reopening reports describe prior near suspension associated with armed/control dispute.
January 5 supported only indirectly in fresh bodies by January 7 two-day retrospective; source for direct start inaccessible.
January 7 activities reportedly resumed after agreement; same TAP lineage in both outlets.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded armed contest concerned control of the crossing, supporting a contextual contested-authority subtype alongside conflict. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Border guard/control dispute and armed intervention security context, not an independently inspected official order.
Tunisian outbound access stopped while Tunisian return admitted; do not claim universal two-way sealing.
Two-day versus more-than-24h wording and asymmetric access prevent exact duration.
